## 1. Channel Progression Strategy

This curriculum organizes the core disciplines of Urban Climate Adaptation across four progressive tiers:
- **Tier 1: Urban Climate Adaptation Foundations & Core Mechanisms (Beginner / Scratch)** — Core physical and conceptual fundamentals, terminology, primary mechanisms, and foundational observation methods in Urban Climate Adaptation.

- **Tier 4: Urban Climate Adaptation Frontier Technologies, Global Impact & Future Horizons (Advanced / Masterclass)** — Emerging technological breakthroughs, policy frameworks, environmental and human impact, and long-term evolutionary projections for Urban Climate Adaptation.

## 3. Topic Catalog (Scratch to Advanced Curriculum)

### Tier 1: Foundational Frameworks
1. **The Architecture of Urban Climate Adaptation: How Urban Climate Adaptation Developed**
   - *Question:* How did a city's risk assessment become an adaptation project?
   - *Key Focus:* Trace one city's adaptation measure from documented hazard assessment through planning and delivery; distinguish historical conditions from projected risk. Evidence base: Trace dated origin records and subsequent interpretations. Case records: local hazard assessments, project designs, maintenance records and observed event performance. Starting framework: IPCC AR6 urban adaptation chapter (https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg2/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGII_Chapter06.pdf).    - *Question:* Did an adaptation project reduce the risk it was designed to address?
   - *Key Focus:* Examine one completed adaptation project using the hazard, exposed population and measured performance; compare results with the original objectives. Evidence base: Read the original evaluation and its population, comparator, outcomes and limitations. Case records: local hazard assessments, project designs, maintenance records and observed event performance. Starting framework: IPCC AR6 urban adaptation chapter (https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg2/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGII_Chapter06.pdf).    - *Question:* Whose exposure or maintenance burden is missing from an adaptation account?
   - *Key Focus:* Document overlooked residents or maintenance workers in one adaptation project; include consented accounts of burdens and uneven protection. Evidence base: Use attributable contribution records and consented participant accounts. Case records: local hazard assessments, project designs, maintenance records and observed event performance. Starting framework: IPCC AR6 urban adaptation chapter (https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg2/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGII_Chapter06.pdf). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..
4. **Urban Climate Adaptation: Understanding Urban Climate Adaptation**

   - *Key Focus:* Explain hazard, exposure, vulnerability and adaptation through one neighborhood; distinguish a planned intervention from demonstrated risk reduction. Evidence base: Use primary definitions and a documented end-to-end example. Case records: local hazard assessments, project designs, maintenance records and observed event performance. Starting framework: IPCC AR6 urban adaptation chapter (https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg2/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGII_Chapter06.pdf). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..

Evidence base: Compare original methods, assumptions, measures and uncertainty. Case records: local hazard assessments, project designs, maintenance records and observed event performance. Starting framework: IPCC AR6 urban adaptation chapter (https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg2/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGII_Chapter06.pdf). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..

Evidence base: Compare competing explanations and specify missing discriminating evidence. Case records: local hazard assessments, project designs, maintenance records and observed event performance. Starting framework: IPCC AR6 urban adaptation chapter (https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg2/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGII_Chapter06.pdf). Evidence base: Trace the process, custody transfers and assigned responsibilities. Case records: local hazard assessments, project designs, maintenance records and observed event performance. Starting framework: IPCC AR6 urban adaptation chapter (https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg2/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGII_Chapter06.pdf).
